question.text:
The domain of the real valued function
$f(x)=\sqrt{\frac{2 x^2-7 x+5}{3 x^2-5 x-2}}$ is

solution.text: Given function $f(x)=\sqrt{\frac{2 x^2-7 x+5}{3 x^2-5 x-2}}$ Here, $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ should be greater than or equal to 0 . So, $2 x^2-7 x+5=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad 2 x^2-5 x-2 x+5=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad(x-1)(2 x-5)=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad x=1, \frac{5}{2}$ $3 x^2-5 x-2=0 \Rightarrow 3 x^2-6 x+x-2=0$ $3 x(x-2)+1(x-2)=0 \Rightarrow(x-2)(3 x+1)=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad x=2, \frac{-1}{3}$ When we include $x=\frac{-1}{3}, 2$ then $f(x)$ would give not define value so, we will exclude these values from the domain. When we take values between $\left(-\frac{1}{3}, 1\right)$ and So, domain is $\left(-\infty, \frac{-1}{3}\right) \cup[1,2) \cup\left[\frac{5}{2}, \infty\right)$
